messages.subject: weird densities estimates in CDS
parts:
Hi all,

I have been trying to analyse data on howler monkey densities (8 transects, range 0.1 to 1.1 km) in a atlantic forest fragment (266 ha).  I got over 58 groups sightings and I discarded (truncated) the largest 10% . I ended with 55 observations. My problem is, I have run the analyses twice with the very same data and I got completly different results!!!  I found distance sampling program extremely unfriendly (I am teaching myself how to use it, and I´d loveto see one day a  manual/guide of "distance sampling for dummies" ). Many times I just do not know what is going on or how small details in how one enter the data could affects the results...

I will appreciate any help in this matter!  Could this be a bug in the system??? I am attaching the files with the data, maybe it would help...

Thank you in advance

When I run the first analyses data were imported as they were entered in excel (a) and in the second case (b) I ordered the data by transects (line, 1, line 2, line 3 and so on).

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] weird densities estimates in CDS
parts:
Antonio:

Sorry you are struggling with the program.  Take the time to read the Users Guide to Distance that comes with the program; there is much useful information there.  For example, Chapter 5, entitled "Data in Distance" contains a section entitled "Introduction to Data Import" in which it states: "While the order of the columns is not important, the order of the rows is. Before importing data into Distance, you should sort by stratum label (if you’re importing more than one stratum), then sample (transect) label. This ensures that all data from the same strata are together, and within this all data from the same sample  (transect) within strata are together. The order of observations within samples is not important."

Indeed the second method, in which you have sorted your data by transects, is the correct way to import your data, and will provide you with the correct results.

Let us know if you run into further difficulties.
